title: The opponent's best resource

D0.outcome: Explains that analysis is not finished until the opponent has had his best reply, including quiet and defensive moves.

D1.outcome: For a given line, lists the opponent's check, capture, threat and best defensive move at each step.

D2.outcome: In unlabeled positions, finds the refutation when the first-choice line has a hidden defensive resource, and accepts the line when none exists.

D3.outcome: In positions where several natural defences look alike, tests each and finds the only move that holds; predicts how a small change makes a second defence work.

misconceptions: If I can't see a defence, there is none.
The opponent will play the move my line expects.
sources: docs/curriculum-map-v1.md §2 S4 (Kotov, Aagaard, Ramesh, Dvoretsky, Rowson, Heisman, all [R] in the map)

sources/sheets/emlasker_common-sense.md §4.16 (find the only defence; do not trust an unverified perpetual)
conditions: Applies to every line chosen for a critical decision.
Several natural defences look similar and only one holds.
contrasts: A combination judged unsound without noticing the quiet follow-up that makes it work (the champion's own game).
Assuming the opponent's reply is the one the line needs.
Forced mate lines where all defences are enumerated.
